newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-SPARTAK STRETCH LEAD AT THE TOP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTAK STRETCH LEAD AT THE TOP.

text.p: Spartak Moscow stretched their lead in the Russian premier league to two points on Saturday with a 3-0 demolition of Chernomorets Novorossiisk.
Second-placed Rotor Volgograd were held 1-1 at home by Krylya Sovietov, who turned up in Rostov more than two hours late for the kick-off.
Spartak were 2-0 up in the space of 11 minutes and a 75th-minute strike from captain Ilya Tsymbalar completed the rout to put the champions on 13 points from five games.
Rotor Volgograd are now two points behind the leaders and they must have had thoughts of a walkover in mind when the visitors from Samara failed to show up for the kick-off.
Hoping to save the cost of a hotel, Krylya decided to fly to Volgograd, 600 kms (375 miles) away, and back on matchday.
Bad weather held up their flight and the game finally kicked off nearly two and a half hours late.

Dynamo Moscow drew level on 10 points with Krylya Sovietov and Rostselmash Rostov after beating the latter 1-0 in the capital. A goal from defender Andrei Ostrovsky just before halftime proved decisive.
Last year's runners-up Alania Vladikavkaz could only manage a goalless draw at home to Baltika from Kaliningrad, and lie eighth with seven points.
Newly-promoted Fakel Voronezh broke their duck this season, securing their first points with a worthy 1-0 win at home to Lokomotiv Moscow.
